maison.title: Letters from the atelier.
maison.intro_paragraph_1: We do not measure perfume in millilitres. We measure it in seasons, in the precise hour at which a flower decides to open, in the silence of cellars where copper and oak slowly teach an oil how to speak. Time, here, is the first ingredient — and the most expensive.
maison.intro_paragraph_2: What follows is not a brochure. It is four short letters from inside the workshop: the fields at dawn, the alembic at noon, the long sleep of maceration, and the final ceremony of pouring an essence into glass. Read them slowly. The fragrance, like the prose, was never meant to be rushed.

recolte.title: The fields wake before us.
recolte._image_query: rose damascena harvest dawn dark mood
recolte.image_alt: Rose damascena petals gathered at dawn in a wooden basket.
paragraphs: Before the sun decides where to stand, the pickers are already kneeling. Damascena needs to be cut while the dew still owns its weight; a single hour later and the rose has forgotten itself. We do not own these fields in Grasse, in the Isparta valley, in the white plains of Mysore. We borrow them from the night, and the night charges its rent in patience.

A kilogram of pure rose absolute will ask for nearly five tonnes of fresh petals — a small mountain of colour reduced to a thimble of soul. The hands that do this work are almost always the hands of women, and almost always silent. There is a kind of prayer in pulling a flower so that the stem does not bruise.

We have learned, after years, to trust the pickers more than the calendar. When they say the harvest will begin on a Tuesday, it begins on a Tuesday, regardless of what we have written in the catalogue. The flower, after all, is the only honest contract.
By eleven in the morning the heat has decided. Whatever we did not gather is already lost to the perfume, and now belongs entirely to the bees.
recolte.pull_quote: A flower picked one hour too late has already begun to forget its own name.

alambic.title: Copper learns the language of steam.
alambic._image_query: antique copper alembic distillation steam dark
alambic.image_alt: Antique copper alembic reflecting low light during distillation.
paragraphs: The petals arrive at the still in shallow wooden crates, still warm, still slightly damp from the field. They are weighed, then poured into the copper belly of the alembic — an instrument designed in the medieval workshops of Andalusia and improved, almost imperceptibly, every century since. Copper, unlike steel, listens.

Heat is applied carefully, the way a musician approaches a long note. Too quickly and the rose burns; too slowly and the perfume falls asleep before it can rise. Steam climbs through the petals, gathers their oil, condenses in the swan-neck, and falls — drop by drop, hour by hour — into a glass receiver below.

Eight kilograms of flower will, after a full afternoon, yield perhaps a teaspoon of clear, almost colourless essential oil that smells, improbably, like everything the field was promising at dawn. Alongside it, a fragrant water — the hydrolat — which our perfumer keeps for his own private formulas and almost never sells.
We have one master distiller. He talks to the copper. He insists it answers.
alambic.pull_quote: The fire does not transform the rose; it only convinces the rose to remember itself.

maceration.title: Months of silence, then a single yes.
maceration._image_query: wooden barrels cellar dim slow time amber
maceration.image_alt: Aged wooden barrels resting in a dim cellar.
paragraphs: Once the perfumer has composed his formula — a long argument between top, heart and base, sometimes resolved in an afternoon, sometimes resisted for years — the perfume is poured into glass and locked away. The cellar is kept at a constant fourteen degrees, slightly humid, almost completely dark. Light, like haste, is an enemy.

What happens in those weeks cannot be photographed. The molecules negotiate. Aldehydes that arrived too loud become considerate. Resins that seemed reluctant find their counterpart. A formula that smelled merely correct on day one will, by week eight, begin to smell inevitable. This is the difference between a perfume and an aroma.

Some of our compositions require sixteen weeks. The oud-based ones require six months. We have never released a perfume on a deadline, because there is no such thing as a deadline that a molecule is willing to honour. The cellar decides. We obey, and we wait.
When the perfumer at last unlocks the cabinet, lifts a vial to the light and breathes — and says nothing for a long moment — we know we are almost ready.
maceration.pull_quote: Patience is not a virtue in our cellar. It is the only available material.

flacon.title: Each bottle signed, numbered, sealed.
flacon._image_query: perfume bottle hand-numbered atelier wax seal candlelight
flacon.image_alt: Hand-numbered amber perfume flacon sealed with gold wax.
paragraphs: The flacons arrive from a small glassworks outside Murano, where the same family has been blowing crystal since the seventeenth century. Each one is heavier than it looks; each one carries, near the base, a tiny inclusion of gold leaf, which the maker insists is not decoration but identification.

The bottle is filled by hand, slowly, with a long-stemmed pipette. Air, in any measurable quantity, is the third enemy of perfume — after light and haste — and we treat every millilitre as if it were the last. The bottle is then weighed, capped, and pressed with a warm wax seal the colour of dark honey.

On the underside of each flacon, in fine engraved script, the perfumer writes a number. Three digits, never more. When the third digit closes a batch, the formula goes back into the cellar, the cellar locks the cabinet, and we begin again from a field, in another season, in another country.
What you uncork at home was, two years ago, a rumour kneeling in the dew. That is the only marketing we are willing to do.
flacon.pull_quote: We do not produce perfume. We finish a conversation that began in a field two years before.

perfumeur.title: THE PERFUMERS · HANDS BEHIND THE BOTTLE
perfumeur.intro: Three noses, three geographies, one obsession. Every bottle in our atelier carries the silent signature of the hand that composed it. Meet the perfumers we trust with our matter.
perfumeur.label: PERFUMER

vasseur.name: Antoine Vasseur
vasseur.bio_1: Trained at ISIPCA in Versailles, Antoine spent eleven years inside the houses of the Marais before stepping out to compose in silence. He works in oils alone, never in alcohol, until the final week of a composition.
vasseur.bio_2: His palette is the Atlantic at dusk: iodine, wet leather, fig wood and the smell of stone after rain. He composes slowly, in twelves and twenty-fours, and rarely accepts more than three commissions a year.
vasseur.bio_3: We met him in 2023 in a converted printer's workshop in Pantin. He had been waiting, he said, for a maison that did not yet exist.

elkhoury.name: Yasmin El-Khoury
elkhoury.bio_1: Born in Beirut, trained in Grasse, Yasmin returned to the Levant after fifteen years in the south of France. She works from a small atelier above the old port, with the windows always open.
elkhoury.bio_2: She composes from memory before formula. A grandmother's pantry, the cedar of a mountain shutter, a slow Sunday in Hamra. Her perfumes carry the structure of a Lebanese poem: dense, allusive, generous in the throat.
elkhoury.bio_3: Her work has been worn quietly by the same forty collectors for over a decade. We are honoured to bring three of her compositions, for the first time, beyond their walls.

belaid.name: Maurice Belaïd
belaid.bio_1: Maurice is the youngest of the three, the most architectural in his thinking. Half Moroccan, half French, raised between Marrakech and Lyon, he treats each composition as a building: foundations, load-bearing notes, ornament.
belaid.bio_2: He is fluent in oud — the resin, the wood, the smoke — and equally fluent in its restraint. He once told us that the difficulty of oud is not in adding it, but in knowing when to stop.
belaid.bio_3: We commissioned him to compose our flagship in 2024. The piece is called Tariqa. It is, to us, the truest sentence the maison has yet written.

bespoke.title: BESPOKE
bespoke.subtitle: A fragrance designed only for you.
bespoke.intro_1: A bespoke composition is not a fast object. It begins with a conversation, often two, sometimes three. We listen for places, weather, people, the smell of a particular room in a particular year.
bespoke.intro_2: From that, the perfumer works in private for six to twelve months. You receive samples, you respond, the formula moves. When it is finished, you receive between thirty and one hundred millilitres in a flacon engraved with your name, and the formula sealed in our archive.
bespoke.intro_3: We accept no more than twelve commissions a year. We invite you to write to us below.

process.title: THE THREE MOVEMENTS
process.step_1_body: A long conversation. We listen for the weather, the people, the rooms that you want to keep.
process.step_2_body: Six to twelve months of work in private. Samples travel between you and the perfumer until the formula settles.
process.step_3_body: Your flacon, hand-engraved, in thirty to one hundred millilitres. The formula sealed under your name in our archive.

privacy.title: PRIVACY
privacy.intro: Perfumes Dubai S.L. — a company registered in Spain and operating a boutique in Dubai — is committed to protecting your personal data with the same patience we apply to our compositions. This policy describes what we collect, why, and how you may exercise your rights.

sections.s1_body: We collect only what is necessary: your name, email, phone (if you share it), shipping address if you order, and the messages you send through our forms. We do not buy data from third parties and we do not enrich your profile from external sources.
sections.s2_body: Article 6.1.b of the GDPR (performance of a contract) for orders and bespoke commissions. Article 6.1.a (consent) for the newsletter. Article 6.1.f (legitimate interest) for fraud prevention and service improvement.
sections.s3_body: Order data is retained for ten years for accounting purposes under Spanish law. Newsletter data is retained until you unsubscribe. Bespoke commission archives are retained indefinitely, at the client's request, since the formula belongs to them.
sections.s4_body: Our boutique operations in the United Arab Emirates may require limited transfers of your data outside the European Economic Area. These transfers are governed by Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission.
sections.s5_body: You may access, rectify, delete, port or restrict the processing of your data at any time. You may also withdraw your consent for the newsletter with a single click. To exercise these rights, write to privacy@perfumesdubai.com.
sections.s6_body: Data Protection Officer · privacy@perfumesdubai.com. You may also lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD).

terms.title: TERMS
terms.intro: By using this site or purchasing from Perfumes Dubai, you accept the terms below. We have written them in plain language, but they remain legally binding.

sections.s1_body: Your visit, registration or purchase constitutes acceptance of these terms as they appear on the date of your action.
sections.s2_body: Every image, text, formula, name and visual identity on this site is the property of Perfumes Dubai S.L. or its perfumers. No reproduction is permitted without prior written consent.
sections.s3_body: Our perfumes are made in small batches and may vary slightly between bottles. This is the nature of natural materials and we consider it part of the object. Allergen lists are included with every order.
sections.s4_body: Prices are shown in EUR, USD or AED according to your selection. Taxes and shipping are calculated at checkout. We reserve the right to modify prices at any time.
sections.s5_body: By European and UAE consumer law, perfumes once opened cannot be returned. Sealed bottles may be returned within fourteen days of receipt, in their original packaging, at the buyer's expense.
sections.s6_body: The courts of Madrid, Spain, have jurisdiction for clients in the European Union. For clients in the United Arab Emirates, disputes are resolved through arbitration in the Dubai International Arbitration Centre (DIAC) under UAE law.

cookies.title: COOKIES
cookies.intro: We use the smallest number of cookies that allow this site to work. We do not track you across the open web.

sections.s1_body: Session cookie, language preference, currency selection, cart contents. These are required for the site to function and cannot be disabled.
sections.s2_body: Aggregate, anonymous traffic information through Vercel Analytics. No personal identifiers are stored.
sections.s3_body: None, by default. Should we ever introduce them, we will request your explicit consent through a banner before any cookie is set.
sections.s4_body: You may clear your cookie preferences at any time by removing the pd-cookies-ack key from your browser storage, after which the banner will reappear on your next visit.
